findings.message: contains multiple layers of encoding (hex/base64/unicode escapes)
findings.remediation: Avoid multi-layer encoding; it hindles review and may indicate malicious intent.
findings.impact: Multi-layer encoding (hex/base64/unicode) significantly hinders security review.
findings.attack_vector: Chained decoding layers — attacker increases analysis cost and may hide malicious payloads.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: references an operating-system persistence mechanism (3 occurrences in this file)
findings.remediation: Document and require explicit user approval for persistent operating-system changes.
findings.impact: Operating-system scheduler, service, or Run-key mechanisms can make plugin behavior persist across sessions.
findings.attack_vector: Source references a conventional persistence mechanism; a separate direct command or write may be required to activate it.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Remove embedded credentials, rotate exposed secrets, and load them only from a protected secret store.
findings.impact: Hardcoded API keys/tokens can be exfiltrated by anyone with read access to the plugin source.
findings.attack_vector: Secret key pattern matched in source — key is shipped in plaintext to all consumers.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: dynamically imports code from a variable path
findings.remediation: Use static imports with allowlisted modules; avoid dynamic import() with variable arguments.
findings.impact: Dynamic import() with variable paths allows loading arbitrary modules at runtime.
findings.attack_vector: import(variablePath) — attacker controls the path to inject malicious modules.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: passes a plaintext HTTP destination to a network API
findings.remediation: Use HTTPS and keep TLS certificate verification enabled.
findings.impact: Disabling TLS verification or using plaintext HTTP allows MITM interception of all traffic.
findings.attack_vector: rejectUnauthorized: false or http:// URL — attacker can intercept/modify all requests.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
